bayesAgriFlow 1.3.0

bayesAgriFlow provides a unified, design-aware Bayesian workflow for agricultural and biological experiments. Version 1.3.0 preserves the frozen 1.2.0 line and adds Remote-Sensing Bayesian Models for analysis-ready UAV, satellite, proximal-sensor, and field-phenotyping workflows. The module reuses the established spatial, spatiotemporal, measurement-error, prediction, and decision layers rather than creating a separate image-analysis architecture.

What 1.3.0 adds

Version 1.3.0 starts after sensor-specific preprocessing. It accepts analysis-ready tabular features and optionally interoperates with terra::SpatRaster and sf for explicit extraction. It adds common vegetation indices, lightweight sensor-reference calibration, Bayesian phenotyping models, multi-sensor fusion, known predictor-error propagation, posterior uncertainty summaries, map-ready outputs, and posterior change between acquisition times. terra, sf, brms, and CmdStan remain optional capabilities and are never installed silently.

Remote-sensing data and indices 

d <- bayes_teaching_data("uav")
rs <- bayes_rs_data(d, "x", "y", id = "plot_id", source = "uav")
z <- bayes_rs_indices(d, nir = "nir", red = "red", blue = "blue", red_edge = "red_edge")

Design-aware phenotyping 

des_rs <- bayes_rs_phenotype(
  d, trait = "biomass",
  features = c("ndvi", "ndre", "canopy_height"),
  x_coord = "x", y_coord = "y", block = "block"
)
bayes_plan(des_rs)

Known sensor uncertainty 

des_me <- bayes_rs_model(
  d, "biomass", "ndvi",
  predictor_sd = c(ndvi = "ndvi_se"),
  spatial = FALSE
)

When the optional brms route is fitted, the error-prone predictor is represented through an explicit latent mi() submodel.

Multi-sensor fusion 

f <- bayes_teaching_data("sensor_fusion")
des_fusion <- bayes_rs_fusion(
  f, "biomass",
  sources = list(
    uav = c("uav_ndvi", "height"),
    satellite = "sat_ndvi"
  ),
  x_coord = "x", y_coord = "y"
)

Posterior maps and change 

if (FALSE) {
  fit_rs <- bayes_fit(des_rs, engine = "brms",
                      compute = bayes_compute(backend = "cmdstanr"))
  pred <- bayes_rs_predict(fit_rs, prediction_grid)
  unc  <- bayes_rs_uncertainty(pred, threshold = 5, direction = "below")
  map  <- bayes_rs_map(pred, quantity = "posterior_sd")
  chg  <- bayes_rs_change(fit_rs, two_date_grid, 14, 28, threshold = 0.5)
}

Inherited from 1.2.0: Spatiotemporal Models

The 1.2.0 layer remains available unchanged, including bayes_spatiotemporal(), separable space-time covariance utilities, AR(1) repeated-series structure, posterior forecasting, exceedance probabilities, matched-location change, and monitoring audits. Version 1.3.0 reuses this architecture when remote-sensing acquisitions are indexed by both location and time.

Stable workflow

The package keeps the same public logic established in 1.0.0:

library(bayesAgriFlow)

design <- bayes_rcbd(
  data = bayes_teaching_data("rcbd"),
  response = "yield",
  treatment = "cultivar",
  block = "block"
)

fit <- bayes_fit(design, engine = "native", draws = 4000, seed = 20260826)
bayes_summary(fit)
bayes_predict(fit)

The four inferential layers remain separate: estimation, evidence, prediction, and decision.

New in 1.1.0: Advanced Experimental Designs

Generate and audit response-surface designs 

ccd <- bayes_ccd(
  factors = c("N", "P", "K"),
  center_points = 6,
  type = "circumscribed",
  alpha = "rotatable"
)

bayes_rsm_audit(ccd)

The module supports central composite and Box-Behnken generation, candidate-set A/D/I/G optimal search, matrix-efficiency diagnostics, region sensitivity, multi-criterion ranking, and cost-efficiency summaries.

Compare matrices before field work 

cmp <- bayes_compare_designs(list(
  CCD = bayes_ccd(c("x1", "x2")),
  BBD = bayes_box_behnken(c("x1", "x2", "x3"))
))

Criteria are kept explicit rather than collapsed into a single universal ranking. In particular, determinant-based and integrated-prediction criteria can favor different designs.

Bayesian pre-experimental evaluation 

info <- bayes_design_information(ccd, prior_sd = 2.5, sigma = 1)
assurance <- bayes_rsm_assurance(ccd, target = "precision")

This extends geometry-only design selection toward prior-informed expected posterior precision and simulation-based assurance.

Fit and interpret Bayesian response surfaces 

dat <- bayes_teaching_data("ccd")
des <- bayes_rsm(dat, "yield", c("coded_N", "coded_P"))
fit <- bayes_fit(des, engine = "native", draws = 4000)

can <- bayes_rsm_canonical(fit)
opt <- bayes_rsm_optimum(
  fit,
  bounds = list(coded_N = c(-1.5, 1.5), coded_P = c(-1.5, 1.5))
)

Posterior geometry includes stationary-point uncertainty and probabilistic maximum/minimum/saddle classification. Bounded biological/economic optimization, ridge search, steepest paths, desirability, and sequential augmentation are also exposed.

Pseudoquadratic fertilizer-response models 

d <- bayes_teaching_data("pseudoquadratic")
des <- bayes_pseudoquadratic(
  d, "yield", c("N_code", "P_code"), powers = 0.5
)

Fractional-power terms are created through an identifiable transformed basis and are never silently substituted for the ordinary quadratic model.

Scientific scope inherited from 1.0.0

The stable baseline continues to cover randomized designs, Latin squares, factorial and split-plot families, mixed/repeated/GLMM models, quantitative regression and optima, nonlinear models, splines, Gaussian processes, Bayesian bootstrap, optional BART, spatial field trials, genotype-by-environment models, multivariate outcomes, measurement error, missing data, censoring, ordinal models, finite mixtures, distributional regression, model averaging, projection-predictive selection, utility/regret, EVPI and EVSI.

Optional backends

Heavy software is never silently installed. brms, cmdstanr, rstan, rsm, AlgDesign, BayesFactor, loo, projpred, bridgesampling, PyMC and PyMC-BART remain optional capability providers. Use bayes_capabilities() and bayes_compute_info() to inspect the environment.

Documentation and consolidated public boundary

Version 1.3.0 contains 40 extensive English vignettes spanning the stable 1.0.0 core and the three additive 1.x modules. The module-specific additions are:

  • 1.1.0: v30–v32, Advanced Experimental Designs and Bayesian response surfaces;
  • 1.2.0: v33–v35, Spatiotemporal Models;
  • 1.3.0: v36–v39, Remote-Sensing Bayesian Models.

The package ships 40 frozen simulated agri_*.csv teaching datasets plus the separate briones_martinez_2002_efficiency.csv benchmark asset.

The public bayesAgriFlow line is consolidated at 1.3.0 for this release cycle. Causal inference, mediation, path analysis, CFA, and SEM are intentionally outside this package boundary and are intended for a separate companion package rather than being appended to this release.

Stability and validation

Version 1.3.0 is additive relative to 1.0.0–1.2.0. The consolidated source exposes 136 public functions and 26 registered S3 methods. Formal release validation requires local R execution, the complete historical unit/integration suite, representative optional-backend sampling, all 40 vignette renders, R CMD build, and R CMD check --as-cran on the exact R-built tarball. Static validation alone is not presented as CRAN validation. See inst/dev/LOCAL_VALIDATION_1.3.0.md and inst/dev/PUBLIC_CONSOLIDATION_1.3.0.md.
